standard.coverage: Covered employers under this state's own act, which adopts or matches the federal rate.
standard.note: New Hampshire repealed its own dollar figure in 2011 and now adopts the federal rate by reference (RSA 279:21).

tipped.note: RSA 279:21 sets the tipped cash wage at 45% of the applicable minimum wage: 45% of $7.25 = $3.26 (DOL publishes $3.27). Applies to employees of restaurants, hotels, motels, inns and cabins who customarily receive more than $30/month in tips.

youthAndTraining.label: Federal youth opportunity wage
youthAndTraining.eligibility: Employees under 20, first 90 consecutive calendar days -- 29 U.S.C. 206(g). Not a state figure; carried here because it is the only sub-minimum wage available in this state.

indexation.note: Not indexed; moves only if the legislature (or Congress) moves it.

knownGaps: 45% of $7.25 is $3.2625. DOL's tipped table publishes $3.27 (rounded up); New Hampshire's own poster states the 45% rule rather than a dollar figure. This file carries DOL's $3.27 because rounding DOWN would underpay.
